name: West Australian Current

primary_definition.interpretation: Broad offshore northward subtropical-gyre flow; distinct from coastal southward Leeuwin. Definition supplies no diagnosed axis, numeric endpoint coordinates or physical width.

coastal_study.interpretation: Coastal shelf-edge system and its regional names; its 5500 km winter system length is not transferable to offshore West Australian Current.

seasonal_context_lead.citation: D’Adamo and Onton (2003), MMS-75/2003, dated 15 July 2003
seasonal_context_lead.locator: Section 4 and Figure 12 caption, printed pp. 5 and 21 / PDF pp. 8 and 24
provenance_chain: US Navy (1976) Climatic Atlas of the World
seasonal_context_lead.interpretation: Seasonal branching descriptions are inherited context, not newly acquired velocity geometry. Figure legend includes probable directions/speeds with insufficient data. Original atlas methodology and applicable samples require review.

historical_naming_lead.access: publisher_indexed_abstract_read_2026-10-03; direct publisher full page unavailable; full paper not inspected
historical_naming_lead.interpretation: Abstract describes a cyclonic stream extending northeast from the Naturaliste Plateau and turning poleward at the coast. Its use of West Australian Current differs from the modern offshore northward definition; equivalence remains unreviewed.
historical_naming_lead.citation: Andrews (1977), Eddy structure and the West Australian current, Deep Sea Research 24(12), 1133-1148, doi:10.1016/0146-6291(77)90517-3.

reported_context.sampling: Four cruises in the summers of 1972 and 1973; individual cruise dates unavailable in inspected abstract.

rejected_inferences: No reuse of Leeuwin or 5500 km coastal-system path length.
No conversion of broad eastern Indian Ocean description into physical width or a representative single core.
No use of seasonal 20 S branching context as a universal whole-current endpoint.
No figure tracing or seasonal interpolation from inherited atlas patterns.
No transfer of the 1977 reported 800 km trough extent or 100-200 km cyclonic stream width into modern offshore-current dimensions before identity equivalence and full source methodology are reviewed.
The historical width interval is not a seasonal minimum/maximum range; a 370 m scale depth is not a uniform axis layer.
No substitution of coastal summer Capes/Ningaloo flow or deeper Leeuwin Undercurrent for the modern offshore West Australian Current.
Model particle release boundaries, sector limits and transport agreement are not current endpoint, width-edge or centerline diagnoses.
remaining_gates: Retrieve the full 1977 paper and resolve its poleward cyclonic-stream naming against the modern offshore northward flow; keep its reported dimensions in unadmitted source context meanwhile.
Choose representative layer and time support for a broad flow; consider a diagnostic flow corridor before a centerline.
Retrieve appropriate offshore velocity data and justify northern/southern interface gates independently of coastal-current geometry.
Read original seasonal atlas/data methodology before generating dated or seasonal routes.
Keep physical width, annual extrema and canonical measurement admission unresolved.

modern_pathway_context.citation: Yit Sen Bull and van Sebille (2016), Sources, fate, and pathways of Leeuwin Current water in the Indian Ocean and Great Australian Bight: A Lagrangian study in an eddy-resolving ocean model, doi:10.1002/2015JC011486.
modern_pathway_context.access: Full publisher page retrieved; Introduction and sections 2.1-2.4 read on 2026-10-03; no figures digitized or model data acquired.
modern_pathway_context.locator: Introduction; 2.2 Eulerian TROPAC01 Validation at 32 S; 2.3 Lagrangian Particle Model; 2.4 coastal sectors.
modern_pathway_context.interpretation: Leeuwin, its deeper equatorward undercurrent, and inshore summer Capes/Ningaloo flows are separately named. Subtropical onshore supply and particle connectivity do not diagnose a whole West Australian Current axis.
modern_pathway_context.validation_caution: Section 2.2 reports lower modeled flow speeds compensated by broader flow in transport validation. Agreement of integrated transport does not independently validate width or a centerline.
modern_pathway_context.model_support: TROPAC01 1/10-degree model; 1960-2009 hindcast at five-day temporal means. This is model support, not West Australian Current observation dates.
